_comment: Provider order here does NOT set routing priority — llm_keys.json does. Every provider that appears in llm_keys.json must appear here too, or check_and_log_quota() silently skips it and its usage is never counted. daily_limit values are best-effort free-tier estimates; tune them against your actual plan.

gemini.unit_definition: 1 API call = 1 unit (LLM routing for script generation)
gemini.notes: Google AI Studio free tier. Estimate — varies per model.

flow: 1. Before API call: check quota_usage(provider, today).units_used < provider.daily_limit
2. If at/over limit: skip provider, try fallback chain
3. If under limit: make API call
4. After API call (success or fail): log to quota_usage(provider, date, units_used, error_code)
5. On 429 or explicit quota error: mark provider as capped for that day

error_handling.429_too_many_requests: Mark provider capped, try fallback chain
error_handling.500_server_error: Log error but do NOT count against quota (provider issue, not user limit)
error_handling.timeout: Log error but do NOT count against quota (retry eligible)

reset_logic.daily: At UTC 00:00 (or configured reset_time_utc), clear units_used for that provider

fallback_chains._comment: Informational only. The real order is read from llm_keys.json top-to-bottom.
